clue.text: Taking drug, peel one's bra off — charming!

indicators.note: taking the drug away means its letter is removed from the scrambled pool
off here means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs strips off their bra and is found delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PEEL ONES BRA, less one E for the drug, are rearranged ('off') to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone personable is pleasant and likeable in manner, which is what a charming person is.

clue.text: Celebrated "Shady Bottom" set aside and given to National Trust

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter, and here it is put aside

parts.note: the rapper Eminem's alter ego is Slim Shady
NT is the standard abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A garden feature called Shady Bottom is handed over to a conservation charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady Bottom' looks like a place name; in fact Shady is Eminem, whose last letter M goes. The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated person is famous and distinguished, which is the sense of eminent.

clue.text: Embarked upon argument

definitions.meaning: to ... a task is to begin it vigorously
a quarrel or brief fight, written with a hyphen

explanation.definitionFit: Setting to work means starting on it, and a hyphenated set-to is a short heated quarrel.

clue.text: Teller's raising shift-pattern with second in branch hurriedly moved

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the whole string so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of who works which shift

indicators.note: second in picks out the second letter of the word branch

parts.note: ran means moved quickly

explanation.surface: A bank employee complains about a rota change after a branch was hastily relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Teller's stands for 'is'. 'raising' turns the whole of ROTA + R + RAN upwards, so it reads NARR ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the one who tells a story, so a teller of tales.

clue.text: Small but significant change in fat left Effy shivering with cold

parts.note: butter is a cooking fat

indicators.note: shivering means trembling, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Effy, who used fat and left herself cold and trembling, makes a tiny alteration with big results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like part of Effy's story, but it is the butter. 'shivering' shuffles the next two words plus C for cold, and C has to go into that mix because it lands in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In chaos theory a tiny initial perturbation, like a wing flap, can cause huge consequences far away.

clue.text: Simply because inlays are evenly used …

indicators.note: evenly used means only the even-numbered letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A craftsman explains that his work is simple just because the inlays are spread evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of BECAUSE INLAYS spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something simply is to do it without difficulty, which is the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Leave toper entertaining bar

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the word is held inside Leave toper

explanation.surface: A drunkard is told to leave the pub that is hosting him.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of Leave and the start of toper.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to forbid or block it, which is to bar it.

clue.text: Simply because inlays are evenly used .. (6) / … perspective starts to vary in every way — to the west, for example

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: west is one of the cardinal compass points

explanation.surface: Seen from another angle, things look different every way you face, westward for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the one before, whose text the held clue repeats; only the part after it is this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewpoint is a way of seeing things, a standpoint or outlook.

clue.text: Announce attempt to make larger space in the galley

indicators.note: announce means the words are spoken, so their sound matters, not their spelling

parts.note: try means attempt, and to ream is to enlarge a hole

explanation.surface: A cook declares plans to make the ship's kitchen roomier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galley' looks like a ship's kitchen, but here it is an oared warship. TRY REAM said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient warship rowed by three banks of oars, a kind of galley.

clue.text: Pitch tent

definitions.meaning: to pitch is to slope or tip to one side
an old word for an awning or canopy over a cart or boat

explanation.definitionFit: To pitch is to lean or slant; a tilt is also a cloth cover, like an awning over a wagon.

clue.text: Is course incomplete following nonsense in restaurant?

indicators.note: following says the pieces before it come after the nonsense

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
taken as written

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a series is a course, as of lectures or treatments

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a meal cut short after foolish talk is normal in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: SERIES less its last letter gives SERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in spit-roasted meat; the def reads as a place in which you eat.

clue.text: Hat — tasselled one — shortly to be given to Miss Bryan

indicators.note: shortly means briefly, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a fez is a tasselled hat, the one referred to
Dora Bryan was a British comic actress

explanation.surface: A tasselled hat is soon to be presented to an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to Hat: a tasselled hat is a fez, which loses its Z. Dora Bryan was a much-loved British stage and screen comedienne.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown.

clue.text: Community's borders with central Sweden obscured

parts.note: EC stands for the European Community
lips are edges or rims

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A community's frontiers with mid-Sweden were hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of SWEDEN are ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclipsed means blocked from view, as the moon blocks the sun, so hidden or overshadowed.

clue.text: Special treatment for Twickenham's first 500 fans of Jonny Wilkinson?

indicators.note: special treatment means the letters are handled in an unusual way, so rearranged
first means the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Twickenham gives special treatment to the first 500 supporters of a rugby star.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home of English rugby. Jonny Wilkinson, England's World Cup winner, played at stand-off (fly-half), so he is an example, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonny Wilkinson played in the fly-half position, also called stand-off, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Being disreputable, none of Cameron's party, we hear, has House's heart

indicators.note: we hear means the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: David Cameron led the Conservatives, or Tories, so none of his party is not Tory

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone shady who isn't a Tory still has the heart of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT TORY said aloud gives NOTORI; OUS is the middle of HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means well known for something bad, which is being of ill repute.

clue.text: Regular diathermy's needed in this circumstance

indicators.note: regular means letters taken at even intervals, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Regular heat treatment is required in such cases.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of DIATHERMY give the answer; the def is a stretch, the Latin word meaning likewise or also.
explanation.definitionFit: Item is an old Latin word meaning likewise or similarly, used to introduce another point.

clue.text: Utterly transparent signal

definitions.meaning: a siren or call saying danger has passed

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it means completely clear; as a phrase it is the siren marking the end of an air raid.

clue.text: Tail last of burglars to nick

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word burglars

parts.note: to nick is to make a small cut

explanation.surface: Police trail the last of the burglars, about to arrest him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' suggests arrest or steal, but here it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: King's description in Constant Wonder reworked

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, as the speed of light in physics

indicators.note: reworked means the word is put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch is portrayed in a reworked version of a perpetual marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: C is followed by ROWNED, a rearrangement of WONDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is described as crowned once he has received the crown at his coronation.

clue.text: We hear solver's going to United at Christmas?

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the spelling

parts.note: you'll is the solver going to, and tied means united

explanation.surface: Rumour says the solver is off to see United play at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football team, but it means tied. YOU'LL TIED said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the old name for the festive season around the twenty-fifth of December.

clue.text: Stamp on feathers with ease

parts.note: a die is a stamp for impressing a design, as on coins
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Someone tramples on a pile of feathers without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ease' looks like a description, but 'ease' is the verb, as a storm eases.
explanation.definitionFit: When a wind or noise dies down it lessens and subsides, which is to ease.

clue.text: Some thieves perform in the evening

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few burglars work after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of thieves and the start of perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesper is an old word for the evening star and hence evensong, an adjective for things of the dusk.

clue.text: Careful of new paramour's charm?

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: A careful look at the new boyfriend's appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CAREFUL OF into FOURLEAFC, and LOVER completes it. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare four-leaved plant of the meadow is a traditional good-luck token, a lucky charm.

clue.text: See 22
Metal top fails — getting blame

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which fails and drops away

parts.note: sodium is a soft metallic element

explanation.surface: A metal lid breaks and someone gets the blame for it.
explanation.walkthrough: SODIUM loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is hatred and disgrace attached to someone, the blame and censure they incur.

clue.text: Deficient party leader allowed to access remuneration

indicators.note: to access means to get inside, so these letters go into the pay word

parts.note: income is money received as pay

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word party

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A failing political leader is permitted to get at the pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to access' means getting in: the party leader's initial plus the word for allowed go inside the pay, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomplete is lacking parts, so wanting or deficient.

clue.text: Setter pores over picture

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to con is to study closely

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler studies an image.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is often I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious image or likeness, a picture.

clue.text: Scraps of these in old odes

indicators.note: these points to the answer itself, odd-numbered letters, taken from old odes

explanation.surface: Fragments of these turn up in ancient poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these' refers to the answer: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of OLD ODES spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends are bits and pieces, leftover scraps.

clue.text: 8 suffering depression, spending day in secluded spot

indicators.note: suffering means the word is in a bad way, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, an ancient galley

indicators.note: spending means using up and losing the letter that follows

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: An ancient galley is damaged, sunk, laid up in a quiet backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the 8 down answer into RETIREM; DENT less D adds ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is withdrawal from society, and by extension a place of seclusion.
